hook.text: China, Japan, France, and Spain all compete to build high-speed rail in other countries.

buildup.text: Indonesia chose China for its Jakarta–Bandung line. India chose Japan for Mumbai–Ahmedabad.

discovery.text: These deals include financing, technology transfer, and political influence. Rail is soft power on tracks.

twist.text: Most export projects are years behind schedule and over budget. Different soil, laws, and cultures cause delays.

climax.text: The race to export high-speed rail is really a race for geopolitical influence across Asia and Africa.

punchline.text: High-speed rail exports sell more than trains—they sell alliances.

quiz.question: Why do countries like China and Japan compete to build rail in other nations?
options: Rail exports provide revenue and geopolitical influence
